And Mary Anderson I don't know if you jumped in on that as well. So the purpose there was to provide an update on the state's response and really it was a no no big surprises there in terms of what you've probably have already seen in the media or from some of his previous briefings and news releases. Some of the couple of the key takeaways that I'd like to point out is that certainly Washington State as a whole continues to be you know viewed nationwide as a leader and taking actions early to address this and kind of bend the curve and certainly the statistics that that we were presented on Sunday which are available on the state's Department of Health website. Do you show that in terms of, you know, the growth in the number of cases and things along those lines. Now it's it's not stopping or going away but one of the words that was used it was kind of plateauing in the Puget Sound region. However, in other parts of the state it does continue continue to grow. One of the positive trends is that the number of hospital beds being used there's tremendous, there's a there's a good number of capacity there, though ICU beds are being used at a much higher rate so those are some good signs that they that they see. At the same time the governor pointed out he's not ready to be able to at this point in time move to the next phase. And right now that next phase deadline is two weeks from today, May 4 2020. He did know that as a state you know and used a football analogy he said no we're about at halftime, in terms of where we need to be. However, he also pointed out that he wanted to keep an open mind into, you know, kind of reversing the process that was instituted around what's open and not so open. He did talk about wanting to get the economy open and he wanted to keep not just an open mind, but also wish to hear from, you know, cities, counties, you know, business, labor, etc. in a safe manner. Another key takeaway was, you know, just the trends overall, but also testing, and he noted, or rather I think the staff noted that there was going to be a number of new testing kits coming into Washington State this week, which is very very welcomed. Because right now the number of test kits that we've had as a state has been fairly limited. So in terms of those being tested has been limited as well and it's really been prioritized with health care workers first responders, you know, people obviously showing and things along those lines. So these new test kits are going to open it up and allow more people to be to be tested so some good news there. So, so, so, so again, we'll see what happens on on May 4. At the same time, we also have the ability to reuse and sterilize some existing that masks. However, that is that a only if absolutely necessary. The next our commutation list which is 461. Those are individuals defined as kind of low level offenders.
